The fact object does not flag this directly, you infer it from the`start` date. If`start` equals the fiscal year start, the value is YTD. If`start` equals the quarter start, it is quarter-only. [...] Run this and it returns several fiscal years of Apple revenue under the new tag. 10-Ks filed under ASC 606 typically retag the prior 1-2 years' comparatives, but rarely older periods. To pull a long history, you may need to query both old and new tags. A pipeline starting from a different tag name sees less, for example calling with`SalesRevenueNet` stops at FY2018. Two subtleties are worth calling out in the filter logic above. First, the`fp` field alone is not sufficient for "annual" because 10-K filings also carry quarterly comparative facts that inherit`fp = FY` from the parent filing; a duration check on`start` and`end` catches these. Second, dedupe needs to key off`end`(the period the fact describes), not`fy`(the fiscal year of the filing that reported it); otherwise comparative years collapse into a single row. This marks the end of the storage cycle dominated by smartphones and PCs for over a decade, with AI infrastructure development becoming the new core growth engine.
